title: OpenFGA Check by top-down userset dispatch versus OpenFGA ListObjects by reverse expansion from the user
explanation: The underlying query is group membership through nested usersets, Member(u,g) :- DirectMember(u,g); Member(u,g) :- Member(u,h), SubGroup(h,g), the object-relationship-model membership relation used by systems like OpenFGA. Side 1 encodes OpenFGA's Check API in its default top-down strategy (checkDirect/checkDirectUsersetTuples): it first pushes demand for a queried object down through subgroups (Demand), then builds membership answers Ans back up from the direct memberships of demanded groups. Side 2 encodes OpenFGA's ListObjects API via reverse expansion (readTuplesAndExecute/ReadStartingWithUser): it grows a reachability relation Reach upward from the queried users' direct group memberships through subgroups, with no notion of a queried object. The Hoare triple claims that, restricted to the queried users and queried objects, the two APIs' answers agree — Check's top-down, demand-restricted evaluation and ListObjects' bottom-up reverse expansion compute the same membership relation on the questions actually asked.
preInWords: The precondition is simply true; no constraints are placed on DirectMember, SubGroup, QUser, or Query.
postInWords: Restricted to pairs whose object is in Query, the answer relation Ans produced by OpenFGA's top-down Check equals the answer relation Reach produced by OpenFGA's reverse-expansion ListObjects.
family: production algorithm pair (rate mismatch; two evaluation directions in one codebase; replaces legacy correctness case Example2032)
obstructionExpectation: rate mismatch (reverse expansion climbs one level per round from the user; the top-down check first pushes the demand down and then builds the answers up, about twice the rounds for the same pair); leveled-framework target; with prophecy both containments follow from the fixpoint facts (no leastness needed)
currentEvidence: accepted invariant (Core.json); certificate not yet built
sides: naive compiler: OpenFGA Check, default top-down userset dispatch (checkDirect / checkDirectUsersetTuples), as the demand-driven form of the membership program restricted to the queried users
naive compiler: OpenFGA ListObjects, reverse expansion (readTuplesAndExecute / ReadStartingWithUser) as the membership closure seeded at the queried users
schemaLinking: both sides restricted to the queried objects inside the postcondition; the Check side is restricted to the queried users by its rules, the ListObjects side by its seed

datalog.label: prog_demand
datalog.text:
Demand(x1) :- Query(x1).
Demand(y1) :- Demand(x1), SubGroup(y1, x1).
Ans(x1, y1) :- Demand(y1), QUser(x1), DirectMember(x1, y1).
Ans(x1, y1) :- Demand(y1), SubGroup(z1, y1), Ans(x1, z1).

Reach(x1, y1) :- QUser(x1), DirectMember(x1, y1).
Reach(x1, z1) :- Reach(x1, y1), SubGroup(y1, z1).

datalog.label: rules as stated in the header comment of Input.lean
datalog.text:
Member(u, g) :- DirectMember(u, g)
Member(u, g) :- Member(u, h), SubGroup(h, g)
Demand(g) :- Query(g)
Demand(h) :- Demand(g), SubGroup(h, g)
Ans(u, g) :- Demand(g), QUser(u), DirectMember(u, g)
Ans(u, g) :- Demand(g), SubGroup(h, g), Ans(u, h)
Reach(u, g) :- QUser(u), DirectMember(u, g)
Reach(u, g) :- Reach(u, h), SubGroup(h, g)
